title: Existence of the pinned equivariant polynomial complex
statement: For a prime $\ell$, any normed field $F$ with a normed $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra structure, and any $r\in\mathbf N$, there is a Model in the precise sense of [def-sfb-homogeneous-polynomial-resolution-data]. Thus the monomial internal coproducts carry the specified diagonal lattice action, alternating deletion differential, individual faces and constant augmentation. No contraction or quasi-isomorphism assertion is part of this conclusion.

proof.text: For each $n$, put $P_n(S)=A(S)[y_{a,i}:0\leq a\leq n,\ 1\leq i\leq r]$, with coefficient restriction. This is a sheaf, by [lem-sfb-profinite-coherent-sheaf-criterion]: for a finite disjoint union, finitely many polynomial supports have finite union, so $P_n(\coprod S_j)=\prod P_n(S_j)$. For a surjection $T\to S$, a polynomial on $T$ with equal pullbacks has each coefficient in the equalizer for the sheaf $A$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Descend those finitely many coefficients; coefficients outside that finite support remain zero. Uniqueness is coefficientwise. The empty set gives the zero module. The finite-support description is exactly [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The resulting module sheaf is the coproduct of copies of $A$ indexed by monomials: maps from the summands extend uniquely by $\sum c_m m\mapsto\sum c_m u_m$, naturally on sections. By [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], this identifies it with the internal direct sum $K^n$ and preserves its sections and restrictions. For the equivalence, the site is small in the stipulated coefficient universe; [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] explicitly includes the coherent profinite site and supplies sheafification with its strong symmetric monoidal structure. In particular tensoring a sheafification unit with any presheaf again becomes an isomorphism after sheafification, by the strong monoidal comparison. Thus local equivalences are monoidal, as required by the equivalence node.

proof.text: The polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] defines deletion, insertion of zero, and $T_g:y_{a,i}\mapsto y_{a,i}-g_i$ over $A(S)$. Here $g\in C(S,L)$ and each $g_i\in C(S,F)=A(S)$ through the continuous inclusions $\mathbf Z_\ell\subset\mathbf Q_\ell\subset F$. These inclusions are isometric for the given restricted norm. Substitution fixes coefficients, hence is $A(S)$-linear; it commutes with restriction since $(u^*g)_i=u^*(g_i)$. Step 1 therefore makes these internal linear maps. On generators $T_gT_t=T_{g+t}$ and $T_0=1$, with inverse $T_{-g}$. These equalities give precisely the natural section actions of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module] for the coordinatewise additive lattice [def-sfb-ladic-lattice].

proof.text: Expand $\delta^{n+1}\delta^nf$ on $(y_0,\ldots,y_{n+2})$. For every $0\leq a<b\leq n+2$, omission of $a$ followed by omission of position $b-1$ and omission of $b$ followed by omission of position $a$ give the same polynomial with coefficients $(-1)^{a+b-1}$ and $(-1)^{a+b}$. All terms pair this way and cancel. Thus $\delta^2=0$. Deleting a coordinate and translating all remaining coordinates commute, term by term, so $\delta T_g=T_g\delta$. Constants are fixed by every $T_g$ and $\delta^0(c)=c-c=0$. Hence inclusion of constants, extended by zero outside degree zero, is an equivariant cochain map from $A[0]$.
